verses.1: In the twelfth year of King Yeravam’s reign, Abiya became king over Judah.
verses.2: He ruled in Jerusalem for six years. His mother’s name was Michahiah, who was from Uria in Giv’a. There was a war between Abiya and Yarav’am during his reign.
verses.3: And Abiya prohibited war against the warriors of the army. He chose four thousand men to go into battle. Their total strength was four thousand men. These warriors were selected from among the nobles of the army.
verses.4: And Abiya stood up from the mountain of Samaria, which is located in the mountains of Ephraim. He said, “Listen to me, Yeravam and all of Israel.”
verses.5: Do not know that Jehovah, the God of Israel, has given David a kingdom over Israel for ever, and to his descendants as a covenant.
verses.6: And Joram, son of Nebat, became a servant of Solomon, son of David. He rebelled against his master.
verses.7: And they gathered around him. They were men of strength, sons of Belial. They rushed towards him. Rachabam, the son of Shlomo, rushed towards them. Rachabam was a young man with a gentle heart. He did not become strong before them.
verses.8: And now, you say that you must strengthen yourselves before the queen of heaven, in the hands of the sons of David. But you are a large number, and with you are gold calves, which Yeravam made for you as idols.
verses.9: They were not rejected by the priests of Jehovah; they were sons of Aaron and the Levites. They became priests for you, just like the people of the other lands. Anyone who brings in a ram or a lamb on the morning day, he will be considered a priest before God.
verses.10: And we, the LORD our God, will not abandon him. The priests will serve the LORD, along with the sons of Aaron and the Levites.
verses.11: And they shall offer sacrifices to the LORD morning and evening. They shall also measure out the grain on the pure altar, and they shall pour out the gold into the altar in the evening, just as we keep the offerings of our God. But you have abandoned this practice.
verses.12: And behold, our God, along with His priests and priestesses, will stand before you to bless you, sons of Israel. Do not fight against Jehovah, the God of your ancestors, for you will not succeed in doing so.
verses.13: And Yerav’am turned the enemy away from them. They became in front of Judah, while the enemy remained behind them.
verses.14: And the Jews turned their faces toward them. They saw that there was war ahead of them from both sides. They cried out to Jehovah and to the priests from their courtyards.
verses.15: And the people of Judah divided themselves into groups. In those groups, the people of Judah were united. And God defeated Jerubbaal and all of Israel before Abiyahu and Judah.
verses.16: And the sons of Israel fled from before Judah. God gave them into their hands.
verses.17: And Abiya and his people attacked them with great force. Five thousand men were killed from Israel.
verses.18: And the children of Israel were subdued at that time. And the children of Judah said, “We trust in the LORD, our God.”
verses.19: And Abia followed after Jerubbaal. He took control of many cities from him: Bethel, its suburbs, and all its surrounding areas. He also took control of Efrén and its surroundings.
verses.20: And the power of Joram did not stop even during the time of Abiyahu. Jehovah defeated him, and he died.
verses.21: And Abiya became stronger. He married forty women, and he had twenty children. Additionally, he had sixteen daughters.
verses.22: And all of Avia’s words, his ways, and his teachings are written down in the teachings of the prophet Edo.
verses.23: And Abia lay with his fathers. They buried him in the city of David. His son Asa became king after him. For twelve years, peace reigned in the land.
